rows.title: Stop/activate/wait races tested
rows.evidence: Iteration 4 (delta F5): SharedLifecycle sync core (single lock owns LifecycleState + three-valued GateEffect; every mutation via LifecycleState::apply; CAS+release one critical section). 5 Loom models exhaust interleavings: two activations -> one winner/one release; activate-vs-stop never both-win-and-release; death-vs-stop one fact; no release after SupervisorLost; duplicate cleanup one winner. Harness detects deliberately weakened CAS (3/5 models fail). Gate: RUSTFLAGS=--cfg nono_loom cargo test -p nono --test loom_lifecycle --release. Iteration 6 (delta F7) added scenario 6, so the R05 model set is complete: 7 Loom models. The two new ones cover the durable store's own race - a recovery reconciling a record while another party confirms the same cleanup (exactly one CleanupConfirmed winner; a recovery that observes the cleanup already proven records nothing) and a recovery racing a stop-then-cleanup (never adopt after cleanup). The recovery's read-decide-record is deliberately not one critical section - reconcile() is pure over an already-read state - and these models are what say that gap is safe.

rows.title: Detached sessions/attach survive caller restart
rows.evidence: Iteration 6 (delta F7) landed slice A: durable schema-versioned session store + identity-reconciled recovery (ADR-0001 s6), library-level in crates/nono/src/lifecycle/session_store.rs. SessionRecord v1 (schema_version const 1; a newer version is typed UnsupportedSchemaVersion found by a version probe read before the rest of the shape, never a field-by-field guess) carrying session UUIDv7, generation, ProcessIdentity, process group, LifecycleState, optional ActivationObservation, created/updated wall timestamps and a bounded opaque metadata copy - no product concept, no command line, no environment. Storage: 0700 dir created-or-opened and CHECKED not repaired (not-a-symlink / owned by the effective uid / no group-or-world bits, each typed); dir opened once O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW and every record reached by openat against that descriptor so no later operation re-walks the path; records <uuid>.json at 0600 (explicit fchmod over the umask), first write O_EXCL, updates write-to-temp + renameat in the same dir (temp O_EXCL, 0600, randomized, not a record name), fsync file then dir. Corruption is typed SessionCorrupt{path,why} and enumeration yields one Result per record, so a corrupt record is reported BESIDE its healthy siblings rather than hiding them. Durable prepare persists at Prepared after the gate-ready observation and every later transition updates the record outside the sync_core lock - the record can lag the live state by one step, which is documented and is exactly why recovery reconciles. Ephemeral PreparedSandbox::prepare is unchanged (no store, no file). Recovery: pure reconcile(state, verdict) -> RecoveryDecision {AlreadyVerified | ProcessGone{basis} | StillRunning{survivors} | Unsettled{reason} | Unsupported{reason}}; a cleanup_verified record is AlreadyVerified whatever the probe says (never adopt a reissued pid); a record in a watched state is moved to Failed with SupervisorLost and persisted. Honest limitation, reported not papered over: a recovered process is NOT our child, so waitpid cannot reach it and its exit code/signal are unobservable - RecoveredSession has no wait, returns no SandboxExit and has no killing Drop; it offers kill_group/kill_pid (same targets<=1 refusal as stop) and verify_cleanup_by(deadline) polling until ESRCH. Generations stay at 1 (one-shot session UUIDs; increments are reserved for slice B's re-prepare). Proven: 27 new unit tests + 2 live, each guard removal-detected (record O_NOFOLLOW dropped -> the symlinked record is followed and the decoy is returned; store-dir O_NOFOLLOW dropped -> the store lands on the link's 0755 target; skip-on-parse-failure -> 4 records become 1; schema check deleted -> a v2 record is read as v1; permission check deleted -> a 0755 store is accepted). Live end-to-end: durable prepare -> a caller that crashes (test-only abandon: gate closed, no kill, no reap) -> fresh SessionStore::open -> the record still says 'prepared' -> recover reconciles it to ProcessGone{PidAbsent} -> verify_cleanup ConfirmedAbsent -> the record reads cleanup_verified. Pending for slice B: detached supervisor that keeps exit facts observable across a restart, attach, and the re-prepare flow that increments generation. Linux verification still blocked (R07). || Iteration 8 (delta F9) landed slice B: the detached supervisor, per docs/adr/0002-detached-supervisor.md. THE MECHANISM, and why it is shaped this way: a library has no binary of its own to re-exec, and forking a LONG-RUNNING supervisor out of a threaded caller is undefined-behaviour territory (allocator locks held by threads that no longer exist; the macOS ObjC runtime aborts outright). ADR-0001's gate child survives fork only because it is syscall-only until execve. So the supervisor is THIS BINARY RE-EXECUTED, opted into by one line of embedder cooperation - nono::lifecycle::supervisor_entry() as the FIRST statement of main(). No-op without a private environment marker (NONO_LIFECYCLE_SUPERVISOR, documented as protocol not configuration, and REMOVED from the environment before any other work so it can never be inherited by a customer child); with the marker it never returns. TWO FORKS, both under ADR-0001 child discipline (syscalls only over parent-built buffers, ending in execve or _exit): the launcher forks an intermediate which forks the supervisor-to-be, writes its pid on the handshake and _exit(0)s - so the supervisor is reparented to init and a long-lived launcher never accumulates a zombie it cannot be expected to reap (this was found by test (g), which could not observe the supervisor's death until the double fork was added); the supervisor-to-be setsid()s, points 0/1/2 at /dev/null, forks the CUSTOMER CHILD through the unchanged child_main, writes a bootstrap blob, clears close-on-exec on its five survivors, sweeps every other descriptor (close_inherited_descriptors extended from a pair to a sorted set), and execve()s. execve replaces an IMAGE and not a PROCESS, so the customer child is still the child of the same pid afterwards - which is the entire reason a detached run's exit facts are directly observable via waitpid. NOTHING ABOUT THE PLAN CROSSES THE EXEC: exec image, argv, environment and platform policy are built and used on the launcher's side, so a CapabilitySet is never serialized and re-trusted across a boundary. SECRETS: the gate release/abort pair travels on a private bootstrap pipe (the customer child already holds it) and is zeroized after parse; the ACTIVATION TOKEN is drawn IN THE SUPERVISOR after the exec and handed back on the readiness handshake, so it never exists in the customer child's address space at all - strictly stronger than the attached path, where it exists between fork and exec. NO BIND RACE: the launcher binds and listens on <store>/<session>.sock (unlink-guarded, 0600 inside the 0700 store, sockaddr_un length REFUSED not truncated) BEFORE the fork and passes the LISTENING descriptor through the exec, so readiness implies a socket that has been listening since before the supervisor existed. Readiness is a byte-tagged handshake carrying the supervisor's own ProcessIdentity and the token, poll-bounded; a binary whose main lacks the hook fails closed at a 20s deadline with PrepareError::SupervisorUnresponsive WHICH NAMES THE FUNCTION. SUPERVISOR LOOP: single-threaded poll over {listening socket, held child's status descriptor, SIGCHLD self-pipe with an errno-preserving handler, connected client}; ONE CLIENT AT A TIME (a second is sent a typed ControlRefusal::Busy and closed, never queued - attach single-client discipline is reserved for slice C); child exit observed by a new ActivatedSandbox::try_wait (waitpid WNOHANG) so a wait never parks the one thread; every transition and the SandboxExit persisted; serving continues after a client detaches; the process exits on CleanupVerified or after IDLE_AFTER_TERMINAL_GRACE (300s, documented on the constant) with a terminal state and nobody connected. PROTOCOL V1 (lifecycle/protocol.rs): u32-LE length-prefixed frames, MAX_CONTROL_FRAME_BYTES = 64 KiB checked FROM THE PREFIX BEFORE A BYTE OF BODY IS READ OR ALLOCATED; hello first in both directions carrying {version, session, generation} each checked on both sides; ops Activate{token[32]} / Wait{deadline_millis} / Stop / Status / VerifyCleanup / Goodbye; replies carry the module's EXISTING typed results (ActivationError, StopError, SandboxExit, CleanupVerification, LifecycleState) rather than rendered strings, which is why ActivationError and StopError gained serde derives; peer-uid checked at accept by REUSING supervisor::socket::peer_credentials (no duplicate mechanism) with a foreign uid closed WITHOUT A WORD, since answering would confirm the session exists; the token is compared supervisor-side by the existing gate digest, never persisted, and redacted from ControlRequest's hand-written Debug. EVERY read and write on BOTH sides is poll-deadline-bounded, closing ADR-0001's unbounded-read residual for this path. CLIENT: DetachedSession::{activate, wait, stop, status, verify_cleanup, detach} - dropping it closes a socket and the run carries on, the opposite of every other handle in the module. RECORD SCHEMA V2 (docs/lifecycle/session-record-v2.md): adds supervisor: Option<ProcessIdentity>, exit: Option<SandboxExit> (witnessed exit facts, durable across a caller restart - the thing slice A could not give), and events: Vec<LifecycleEvent> (bounded ring, DETACHED_EVENT_RING_CAPACITY = 32, oldest dropped). The ring is the HONEST representation of a real limit: EventSink is caller-side by design, so events observed while nobody is connected are NOT deliverable live and are not pretended to be. V1 COMPATIBILITY IS EXPLICIT, NOT LENIENT: the version probe chooses between two deny_unknown_fields shapes, a v1 record is parsed as v1 and upgraded IN MEMORY (no supervisor, no exit, empty ring - absence reported, never invented), the file is untouched until something writes it, and a version neither shape implements is still UnsupportedSchemaVersion. RECOVERY: reconcile gains a third pure input SupervisorPresence {NeverDetached, Alive, Gone} (fail-closed through ProcessIdentity::is_same_process) and a RecoveryDecision::Attachable that outranks every child probe but NOT AlreadyVerified (a proven cleanup stays terminal); an attachable record is NOT moved to Failed, because the live supervisor owns it and a second writer would be the exact hazard the store exists to avoid; a Gone supervisor's stale socket is unlinked by the store at the point its staleness was established by identity rather than guessed from a failed connect. SUPPORT REPORT: detached_supervisor is now Available/PlatformApi with the entry-hook PRECONDITION spelled out in reason.why_not_probed (a probe would have to launch a supervisor: two forks, an exec, a bound socket and a durable record), and attach is Partial - control attach landed, TERMINAL attach did not. STATED LIMITS, not omissions: a headless detached run's standard streams are /dev/null (a supervisor holding its launcher's pipes is the thing detachment is for; giving output back is slice C's PTY); gate expiry stays lazily evaluated at the next control operation, exactly as on the attached path, so an abandoned never-activated detached session holds its supervisor until the plan's activation_expiry is reached at that next operation. PROVEN: 32 new unit tests + a new harness=false integration target crates/nono/tests/lifecycle_detached.rs (15 live, 1 ignored per R18) whose own main() installs the entry hook - libtest owns main and offers no pre-main hook, and the same main is what makes the core proof possible. THE R09 CORE PROOF (test b): the test binary re-runs ITSELF with a private flag as a launcher, that launcher prepares a detached session, prints the session id and token, and EXITS; the main test process - which forked nothing involved - opens the store, recover() answers Attachable, attach() connects, activate() releases the child with a token that crossed a process boundary, and wait() returns Exited{0}/Observed witnessed by waitpid IN THE SUPERVISOR. Also proven live: activate/wait/verify end to end; exit observed while fully detached and read back after reconnect; stop-before-activation with activation-after-stop refused as a typed AlreadyStopped over the wire; replayed Activate refused as AlreadyActivated by the gate's own state machine (not by the protocol); wrong protocol version, wrong session, wrong generation, oversize frame, garbage frame, operation-before-hello and second-concurrent-client all refused with typed frames and closed; SIGKILLed supervisor leaves a stale socket that recover() removes before falling back to the slice-A cleanup path. REMOVAL-DETECTED: hello version check deleted -> the wrong-version client is GREETED instead of refused; frame-length bound deleted -> the supervisor reads a body that never arrives and the oversize test fails with 'the supervisor must answer'; stale-socket unlink deleted -> 'recovery must remove the stale socket it just proved dead'; hello-first guard deleted -> a Status sent before any hello is served. Every test-side wait is bounded. PENDING FOR SLICE C: PTY ownership and terminal attach/detach/resize on the same socket with a distinct channel discipline (contract 8), and the re-prepare flow that increments generation (still always 1). Linux verification still blocked (R07): the F9 code is platform-neutral apart from the Linux close_range arm of the extended sweep and has not been executed on a Linux kernel by this stream.

rows.title: Cleanup verification generation/PID-reuse safe
rows.evidence: Iteration 5 (delta F6): typed CleanupVerification landed (ConfirmedAbsent{basis}/StillPresent{survivors}/Indeterminate{reason}/Unsupported{reason}, closed enum, typed evidence payloads; a sent signal is never a basis). Child leads its own process group (setpgid(0,0) in the trusted pre-exec sequence; failure = typed PreExecStage::ProcessGroup), so a reaped run probes kill(-pgid,0) and an unobserved death probes pid+start_time+boot_id. PID-reuse safe: alive-but-different start time => ConfirmedAbsent{IdentityMismatch}; boot change => ConfirmedAbsent{BootIdChanged} (checked before any probe); unreadable start time => Indeterminate, never a proof of absence; targets <= 1 refused before the syscall. Only ConfirmedAbsent records CleanupConfirmed; duplicate verification refused by the state machine. ActivatedSandbox::stop kills the group (and the child pid, for a setsid escapee) and reports the waitpid observation; StopError::SignalFailed is typed. Live-proven on macOS: verify-after-exit, honest StillPresent for a backgrounded grandchild then ConfirmedAbsent after the consumer kills the group, stop()-then-verify, stopped-before-activation verify; removing setpgid makes the survivor test report ConfirmedAbsent while /bin/sleep 30 still runs. 17 unit + 5 live tests. Iteration 6 (F7) added recovered-session verification: RecoveredSession::verify_cleanup reuses the same verdict machinery over the recorded identity/pgid (DeathObservation::NotReaped, because a recovered process was never waited for by anyone here) and only ConfirmedAbsent marks the record CleanupVerified; ActivatedSandbox::drop now kills the process GROUP before the pid, closing the F6 residual. Pending: Linux verification (R07 blocker); documented dark spot - a descendant that calls setsid leaves the group (needs a cgroup-class mechanism).

rows.title: Machine-readable support report
rows.evidence: Iteration 7 (delta F8) landed lifecycle/support.rs. SupportReport::gather() is infallible and returns a tree of Capability<T> = {status: available|partial|unavailable|unknown, determination: probed_live|platform_api|declared, reason: typed (probed | probe_refused | other_platform | platform_api_linked | not_implemented | not_observable_without_irreversible_change | platform_cannot_express), facts: typed or absent}. NO BARE BOOLEAN anywhere in the serialized tree, locked structurally by a test that walks serde_json::Value and rejects Value::Bool at any depth (removal-detected: adding one bool to CleanupFacts fails 3 tests and prints the JSON pointer). Fields: host (compiled target AND uname(2) sysname/release/version/machine; node name deliberately not read - a hostname is not a capability fact), landlock (REUSES upstream Sandbox::detect_abi + DetectedAbi::has_* for a per-right table filesystem_base/refer/truncate/execute/tcp_network/ioctl_dev/scoping - available only if every right is, else partial; zero diff to sandbox/*), seccomp (upstream's own fork-isolated probe_seccomp_block_network_support -> probed_live), seccomp_user_notification (honestly UNKNOWN: SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER cannot be established without installing a filter that cannot be removed from the installing process, and a kernel release number is not proof since CONFIG_SECCOMP_FILTER can be off), seatbelt (PLATFORM_API not probed_live, with the rationale in reason.why_not_probed: sandbox_init is linked so presence is a compile-time fact, but it applies process-wide and irreversibly, so a live probe must fork - the CLI's setup --check-only does exactly that and is not library machinery; asserted by a macOS test), network_filtering (per-mechanism table incl. seatbelt_per_port_tcp = unavailable/platform_cannot_express naming NetworkFilterUnsupported, so the absence is STATED not inferred), pty (live posix_openpt(O_RDWR|O_NOCTTY) closed immediately -> probed_live) kept SEPARATE from interactive_session (not_implemented) so 'pty: available' cannot be misread as 'the lifecycle will give you one', detached_supervisor + attach (unavailable/not_implemented{R09 slice B} - honest, slice B pending), process_identity (captures THIS process and re-checks: start_time/boot_id/self_recognition all probed_live true on this host), cleanup_verification (signal-0 probes of self and own group, reusing cleanup::{probe_pid,probe_group} made pub(crate) so the report cannot drift from the mechanism), event_observation (per-family fidelity map; kernel_denial = NOT_OBSERVED on BOTH platforms - the lifecycle installs no seccomp-notify listener and macOS Seatbelt denials reach userspace only via the system log; the CLI's log-stream reconstruction is explicitly NOT claimed), dark_spots (typed list of the 4 limits already recorded in module docs: setsid group escape, pgid reuse after reap, exec-or-killed EOF ambiguity, Instant-frozen gate expiry - each with consequence + the file that documents it). Upstream SupportInfo{is_supported} untouched. 17 unit tests + docs/lifecycle/support-report-v1.md with a golden example locked by a snapshot test that reads the doc itself. macOS values live-verified; the Linux halves (landlock ABI table, seccomp probe) are written-unverified behind the R07 Docker blocker. || Iteration 8 (F9) updated two entries: detached_supervisor Unavailable/NotImplemented -> Available/PlatformApi with the supervisor_entry() precondition and its typed failure named in reason.why_not_probed (a probe would have to launch a supervisor); attach Unavailable -> Partial, because control attach landed and terminal attach did not. Both are asserted by their own tests and both are in the golden example locked by docs/lifecycle/support-report-v1.md.

rows.title: Generic event delivery for directly observed events
rows.evidence: Iteration 7 (delta F8) expanded lifecycle/events.rs to the contract shape. LifecycleEvent is now an envelope {session_id: Option<Uuid> (always Some in practice), generation, seq: u64, observed_at: SystemTime captured AT observation, identity: Option<ProcessIdentity>, observation: Observation} around a closed what: LifecycleEventKind {StateChanged (kept, so existing consumers keep their fact), PrepareStarted, SandboxApplied, GateReady, ActivationAttempted{outcome}, Released, ExecObserved, ChildExited{outcome}, StopRequested, StopObserved{outcome}, GateAborted, SupervisorFailure{stage,errno}, CleanupVerdict{verdict}, RecordPersisted{schema_version}}. seq is owned by a crate-internal EventEmitter shared by Arc across the prepared->activated handoff, so one run is ONE unbroken sequence (removal-detected: a second emitter restarts at 0 mid-run and fails both live sequence tests); seq is documented as the ordering authority and observed_at explicitly is NOT (a wall clock can step). ActivationOutcome = {Accepted, RefusedWrongSession, RefusedWrongGeneration, RefusedGateClosed{state}, RefusedExpired, RefusedInvalidToken} carries NO token material by construction, locked by a test that walks the serialized tree rejecting any key named token/nonce/secret/digest and ANY array (every secret in the module is a [u8; N]) plus a long-blob check over serde and Debug (removal-detected). No synthesized kernel denials: the vocabulary has no variant for what the platform does not show. Emission points: prepare() -> PrepareStarted (pre-fork, the one event with no identity); the child's gate-ready record -> SandboxApplied + GateReady; activate() -> ActivationAttempted at every outcome, Released after the claim's write, ExecObserved on EOF; wait() -> ChildExited; stop paths -> StopRequested/StopObserved; abort_gate -> GateAborted (only when a live gate was closed); fail_activation -> SupervisorFailure; verify_cleanup -> CleanupVerdict for EVERY verdict, not only ConfirmedAbsent; SessionStore write -> RecordPersisted (never for a write that failed). Every emit is outside the SharedLifecycle lock and after the fact; SessionHandle::persist was restructured to release the record mutex BEFORE calling the sink, so consumer code never runs under a library lock. Rule the order follows: the fact first, then the state change it caused. Proven: 8 new unit tests + 3 live (whole-vocabulary happy run, stopped run reported as stop_requested/stop_observed rather than child_exited, refused activation carrying no token material), each live test asserting the exact sequence, seq gaplessness, observed_at non-decreasing, and identity present on every event after the fork. docs/lifecycle/lifecycle-event-v1.md carries the field table and a golden example locked by a snapshot test. macOS live-verified; the Linux halves are the same code paths behind the R07 blocker. || Iteration 8 (F9) added the honest answer to 'what happens to events when there is no caller'. EventSink stays caller-side and NOTHING was invented to deliver events to a caller that is not there: a detached supervisor installs its own EventRing sink and persists the last DETACHED_EVENT_RING_CAPACITY = 32 events into the session record (schema v2 field), oldest dropped, read back by DetachedSession::status().events(). The fidelity is documented as bounded and lossy in three places (the constant, the record schema doc, and the client module). The one event a supervisor learns about rather than witnesses - a child that ended at the gate while nobody asked - is emitted with Observation::Reconstructed, as is the PrepareStarted of an adopted child, whose fork happened in the launcher before the supervisor image existed.
rows.note: API shape change for consumers: LifecycleEvent went from enum to struct. LifecycleEvent::StateChanged{from,to,observation} is now LifecycleEventKind::StateChanged{from,to} reached via event.what(), with observation on the envelope. Recorded in HANDOFF.md.
